subject: Jiografia na Mazingira

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Master basic map and solar system skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Use maps in everyday life
activities.learning_activity: Explain the concept of geography and environment (meaning, relationship, and importance)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm the meaning of geography and environment
Reading assignment: Guide students to read a reading passage on the relationship between geography and environment and then discuss it
Question and answer: Guide students to explain the importance of geography and environment to their communities
Online and library learning: Guide students to read online or in books content concerning the importance of geography and environment and then discuss
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of geography and environment has been explained correctly
suggested_resources: A chart showing the concept of geography
A video with content on the concept of geography

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Master basic physical relief and existing resources skills
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate basic understanding of physical relief
activities.learning_activity: Explain the concept of physical relief (meaning, landforms - mountains, hills, plains, valleys, plateaus, basins, and distribution)
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Guide students to explain the meaning of physical relief and name landforms
Discussion: Guide students to explain the distribution of landforms using maps
Observation: Take students to nearby areas to observe various landforms
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of physical relief has been explained correctly
suggested_resources: Pictures and charts of various landforms

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Master the basics of environmental conservation
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate basic understanding of environmental conservation education
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the relationship between human activities and environmental conservation (livestock keeping, mining, fishing, lumbering, industries, and agriculture)
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Using questions and answers, guide students to explain the meaning of environment, human activities, and environmental conservation
Discussion: Guide students in groups to discuss the relationship between human activities and environmental conservation
Observation: Guide students to visit school and home areas where human activities take place to identify the existing relationship between those activities and environmental conservation
activities.assessment_criteria: The relationship between human activities and environmental conservation has been explained correctly
suggested_resources: Short videos and articles of real-life examples of human activities affecting the environment and the actual environment

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Master the basics of environmental conservation
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate basic understanding of environmental conservation education
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explain methods of environmental conservation (planting flowers and trees/grass, various methods of waste management in the environment)
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Guide students to explain methods of environmental conservation
Online and library learning: Guide students to read in the library or online about methods of environmental conservation
Observation: Guide students to visit nearby areas with conserved environments to identify the methods used to conserve those environments
Practical work: Guide students to plant trees and flowers/grass and use proper waste management methods
activities.assessment_criteria: Methods of environmental conservation have been explained correctly
suggested_resources: Short videos and articles of events with real-life examples of environmental conservation

activities.main_competence: 1.0 To master basic map-reading and solar system skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 To use maps in daily life
activities.learning_activity: (a) Showing the direction of various objects using the four and eight main cardinal points of the world (identifying the four main points, drawing the four main points, using the four main points to show direction, identifying the eight points, drawing the eight points, using the eight points to show direction)
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Guide pupils using questions and answers to identify the four and eight main cardinal points of the world

Practical work: Guide pupils to (i) draw and show the direction of the four and eight main cardinal points of the world (ii) use the four and eight main cardinal points to show objects and various areas of the school and their communities
activities.assessment_criteria: The direction of various objects has been shown using the four and eight main cardinal points of the world

activities.main_competence: 1.0 To master basic map-reading and solar system skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 To use maps in daily life
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explaining the concept of a map (meaning, features, and importance)
suggested_methods: Questions and Answers: Engage pupils using questions and answers to explain the meaning of a map
Group work: Guide pupils in groups to discuss the features and importance of maps and then present in class
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of a map has been explained correctly

activities.main_competence: 1.0 To master basic map-reading and solar system skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 To use maps in daily life
activities.learning_activity: (c) Drawing a simple map to show the classroom environment
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Guide pupils to identify items found in the classroom
Practical work: Guide pupils to draw a simple map showing the classroom environment
activities.assessment_criteria: A simple map showing the classroom environment has been drawn correctly
suggested_resources: Drawing tools (Paper, pencil, eraser, ruler, manila cards, classroom map)

activities.main_competence: 1.0 To master basic map-reading and solar system skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 To use maps in daily life
activities.learning_activity: (d) Drawing a simple map of the school, ward, district, Tanzania
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss how to draw a simple map of the school, ward, district, and Tanzania
Practical work: Guide individual pupils to draw a simple map of the school, ward, district, and Tanzania
activities.assessment_criteria: A simple map of the school, ward, district, and Tanzania has been drawn correctly

activities.main_competence: 1.0 To master basic map-reading and solar system skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 To use maps in daily life
activities.learning_activity: (e) Using a simple map to determine direction, distance, and to give and follow instructions
suggested_methods: Questions and Answers: Use questions and answers to guide pupils to identify the uses of maps in their daily lives
Practical work: Use simple maps (classroom, school, and village) to guide pupils to determine direction, distance, and to give and follow instructions
activities.assessment_criteria: A simple map to determine direction, distance, and to give and follow instructions has been used correctly

activities.main_competence: 1.0 To master basic map-reading and solar system skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 To use maps in daily life
activities.learning_activity: (f) Using a map to show administrative boundaries (Regions) and relief features (mountains, valleys, rivers, great lakes, and the sea)
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Through questions and answers, guide pupils to identify administrative boundaries and areas or regions where various relief features are found
Presentation: Use the map of Tanzania for pupils to identify things that make up relief features and administrative boundaries
Practical work: Guide pupils to draw the map of Tanzania showing administrative boundaries (regions) and relief features
activities.assessment_criteria: A map showing administrative boundaries and relief features has been used correctly
suggested_resources: Map showing administrative boundaries and relief features

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Master basic skills of landforms and available resources
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Show an understanding of the main natural resources of Tanzania
activities.learning_activity: Explain the distribution of the main natural resources of Tanzania
suggested_methods: Observation: Guide students to identify and explain the resources available in their communities
Online and library learning: Guide students to read various information sources to identify the main natural resources of Tanzania
Discussion: Guide students to discuss the distribution of Tanzania's main natural resources
activities.assessment_criteria: The distribution of Tanzania's main natural resources is explained correctly
suggested_resources: Maps showing the distribution of Tanzania's main natural resources

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Master basic skills of landforms and available resources
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Show an initial understanding of the relationship between natural resources and development
activities.learning_activity: Explain the relationship between the distribution of natural resources and development (forests-tourism, beekeeping; rivers/lakes/oceans-fishing, transportation, agriculture; land-agriculture, livestock keeping, mining)
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Guide students to explain the relationship between natural resources and development
Case study: Guide students to read various cases concerning the distribution of natural resources and their relationship to development
Discussion: Guide students to discuss the distribution of natural resources and its relationship with development
activities.assessment_criteria: The relationship between the distribution of natural resources and development is explained correctly
suggested_resources: Texts with content on the relationship between the distribution of natural resources and development

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Master basic skills of human geography
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Show an initial understanding of the relationship between population distribution and resource use
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the geographical causes of population distribution
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Use questions and answers to involve students in explaining the geographical causes of population distribution
activities.assessment_criteria: The geographical causes of population distribution are explained correctly

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Master basic skills of human geography
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Show an initial understanding of the relationship between population distribution and resource use
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explain the relationship between population distribution, resource use, and environmental conservation
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide students to discuss the relationship between population distribution, resource use, and environmental conservation
activities.assessment_criteria: The relationship between population distribution, resource use, and environmental conservation is explained correctly
suggested_resources: Videos and charts showing the relationship between population distribution, resource use, and environmental conservation

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Master the fundamentals of environmental conservation
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Show an initial understanding of the concept of weather and its relationship to economic activities
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the concept of weather (meaning, weather elements, and equipment used to measure and record weather)
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm the meaning and elements of weather
Discussion: Guide students to discuss the equipment used to measure and record weather elements
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of weather is explained correctly
suggested_resources: Video with content on the concept of weather, and various equipment for measuring weather elements

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Master the fundamentals of environmental conservation
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Show an initial understanding of the concept of weather and its relationship to economic activities
activities.learning_activity: (b) Measure and record temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind, and air pressure
suggested_methods: Field trip: Guide students to visit a weather station in their surrounding areas to measure and record weather elements
activities.assessment_criteria: Temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind, and air pressure are measured and recorded correctly
suggested_resources: Various equipment for measuring weather elements

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Master the fundamentals of environmental conservation
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Show an initial understanding of the concept of weather and its relationship to economic activities
activities.learning_activity: (c) Explain the relationship between weather and economic activities
suggested_methods: Questions and answers: Guide students using questions and answers to explain the relationship between weather and economic activities
Discussion: Guide students to discuss the relationship existing between weather and economic activities
activities.assessment_criteria: The relationship between weather and economic activities is explained correctly
suggested_resources: Text with content concerning the relationship between weather and economic activities

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Master basic map reading and solar system skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate basic understanding of solar system education
activities.learning_activity: Explain the concept of the solar system (meaning, importance, planets and their arrangement, and other celestial bodies)
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Guide pupils using questions and answers to explain the meaning and importance of the solar system
Practical guidance: Guide individual pupils to draw a diagram of the solar system and explain it accurately
Discussion: Guide pupils in groups, using a diagram of the solar system, to discuss the arrangement of the planets
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of the solar system is explained accurately
suggested_resources: cartoons/animated pictures showing the arrangement of the planets

activities.main_competence: 1.0 Master basic map reading and solar system skills
activities.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate basic understanding of solar system education
activities.learning_activity: Online and library learning: Guide pupils to read in the library or online about the sun, planets, and other celestial bodies and then present in class
suggested_methods: Online and library learning: Guide pupils to read in the library or online about the sun, planets, and other celestial bodies and then present in class
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of the solar system is explained accurately
suggested_resources: cartoons/animated pictures showing the arrangement of the planets

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Master basic relief skills
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate basic understanding of relief
activities.learning_activity: Explain the relationship between relief and natural vegetation
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Through questions and answers, guide pupils to explain the relationship between relief and natural vegetation
Discussion: Guide pupils to discuss the relationship between landforms and natural vegetation
activities.assessment_criteria: The relationship between relief and natural vegetation is explained accurately
suggested_resources: Maps showing the relationship between relief and vegetation
animated pictures showing landforms and natural vegetation

activities.main_competence: 2.0 Master basic relief skills
activities.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate basic understanding of relief
activities.learning_activity: Field trip: Guide pupils to identify the relationship between relief and natural vegetation in the natural environment
suggested_methods: Field trip: Guide pupils to identify the relationship between relief and natural vegetation in the natural environment
activities.assessment_criteria: The relationship between relief and natural vegetation is explained accurately
suggested_resources: Maps showing the relationship between relief and vegetation
animated pictures showing landforms and natural vegetation

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Master basic human geography skills
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate understanding of sources of population and settlement data
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the importance of population and settlement data
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Through questions and answers, guide pupils to explain the importance of population and settlement data
activities.assessment_criteria: The importance of population and settlement data is explained accurately
suggested_resources: Text materials containing population and settlement content

activities.main_competence: 3.0 Master basic human geography skills
activities.specific_competence: 3.1 Demonstrate understanding of sources of population and settlement data
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explain the sources for obtaining population and settlement data (census: meaning, types, characteristics, importance, birth and death registration, migration records)
suggested_methods: Discussion: Guide pupils in groups to discuss various sources for obtaining population and settlement data and then present in class
Discussion: In groups, guide pupils to discuss various sources for obtaining population and settlement data
Guest speaker: A guest with knowledge on various sources for obtaining population and settlement data to talk to pupils
activities.assessment_criteria: Sources for obtaining population and settlement data are explained accurately

activities.main_competence: 4.0 Master the basics of environmental conservation
activities.specific_competence: 4.1 Demonstrate basic understanding of the concept of climate and its relationship with economic activities
activities.learning_activity: (a) Explain the concept of climate and factors affecting it
suggested_methods: Question and answer: Through questions and answers, guide pupils to explain the concept of climate and factors affecting it
Case study: Using various scenarios in the community and environment, guide pupils to explain factors affecting climate
Discussion: Guide pupils in groups to discuss human activities affecting climate
activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of climate and factors affecting it are explained accurately

activities.main_competence: 4.0 Master the basics of environmental conservation
activities.specific_competence: 4.1 Demonstrate basic understanding of the concept of climate and its relationship with economic activities
activities.learning_activity: (b) Explain the relationship between climate, population distribution, and economic activities
suggested_methods: Brainstorming: Guide pupils to brainstorm on the relationship between climate, population distribution, and economic activities
Case study: Use various scenarios to explain the relationship between climate, population distribution, and economic activities
Field trip: Guide pupils to visit the actual environment to relate climate, population distribution, and economic activities
Discussion: Guide pupils in groups to discuss the relationship between climate, population distribution, and economic activities
activities.assessment_criteria: The relationship between climate, population distribution, and economic activities is explained accurately
suggested_resources: video showing the relationship between climate, population distribution, and economic activities
